content_of_post_to_comment:
I feel like I’m wasting my youth trapped in a no-motivation loop. There are so many things I want for myself but can’t seem to get myself to start.

- diet

- exercise

- hobbies

- friends

- dating

- sleep

- new experiences

- keep a clean living space

- keep in better contact with loved ones

I don’t have a consistent sleep schedule because I usually work at different times of the day. So my circadian rhythm is always out of whack. That also makes it hard to have a daily routine. I’m either up really late and sleep in until I need to wake up and get ready for a late shift, or I’m waking up super early for a morning shift and exhausted after work and don’t feel like doing anything after.

Im not blaming having a job. That’s great, I’m so grateful I have one! I’m blaming myself for letting the excuses pile up to the point where collectively, they feel like a mountain.

Example day:

I sleep in and then don’t have time to go to the grocery store. No food to cook so I don’t eat enough. Not enough energy to last all day. Finish work hungry and tired. Go home for food and maybe a nap. Can’t workout with no energy, but if I go home after work, I’m in for the night. If I eat out after work I hit a food coma. I don’t feel like dating if I’m underweight/out of shape, so I stay single and lonely. That just makes it harder to meet new friends and have a social life. If nobody is ever coming over, it doesn’t matter if my place is a mess. Laundry and dishes pile up. Any ‘free’ time should be spent doing those first, I can do those tomorrow though. I’ll watch one episode while I eat my microwave dinner. 4 episodes later it’s 2am and I need to sleep. Or I’m up late playing video games with friends from back home with the excuse that it’s just me keeping in touch

Each part of the cycle prevents another part. It all just feels like a lot. I really want to jumpstart my life and get back to being productive and happy. It seems like it should be as simple as telling myself to stop being a bum. But when it comes time to act, I’m easily stopped by easier/more fun things.

Does anybody else experience this?

How did you begin to turn yourself around?
comment: The part about free time becoming either chores or four episodes of a show feels really familiar. Sometimes trying to fix diet, fitness, dating, sleep, and everything else at once makes the mountain even bigger. I’ve found it helps to pick one tiny anchor habit, like groceries on a set day or a 10-minute walk after work, and let the other pieces rebuild around it.
